overview: The Medford City Council met to address traffic safety near the Brooks School, municipal building repairs, health department staffing, and local zoning concerns. Among several actions, the Council passed a first reading of an ordinance raising the legal tobacco purchase age to 21 and approved funding for library roof repairs.

items.title: Commendation for Eagle Scout Andrew Knight
items.summary: The Council presented a commendation to Andrew Knight for attaining the rank of Eagle Scout and creating a recycling center project for the Medford Boys & Girls Club.

items.title: Resolution for Traffic Light and Safety Improvements at High and Alston Streets
items.summary: The Council approved an amended resolution requesting the Mayor install a traffic light and implement traffic calming measures at High and Alston Streets following a pedestrian accident near the Brooks School.

items.title: Public Participation: Excise Tax Dispute
items.summary: Resident Eddie Poria presented concerns regarding a 30-year-old vehicle excise tax bill, and Councilor Knight advised him to petition the Board of Assessors for an abatement.

items.title: Special Permit Hearing for Keno Monitor at 562 High Street
items.summary: The Council opened a public hearing on a special permit petition for a Keno monitor at N.K. Convenience and voted to table the matter for one week.

items.title: Loan Order for City Hall Roof and Facade Improvements
items.summary: The Council tabled a $1,800,000 loan order for City Hall roof, parapet, and facade renovations pending further review.

items.title: Free Cash Appropriation for Library Roof Repairs
items.summary: The Council approved a $45,000 free cash appropriation to perform necessary weather-tight repairs to the Medford Public Library roof.

items.title: Free Cash Appropriation for City Hall Roof Contract
items.summary: Action on a $1,200,000 free cash appropriation for Phase 1 City Hall roof repairs was delayed after Councilor Marks invoked Rule 20.

items.title: Resolutions on Police Presence, Truck Restrictions, and Illegal Dumping
items.summary: The Council approved resolutions requesting increased police presence in Medford Square, truck restrictions on Harvard Avenue, and fencing to curb illegal dumping on Commercial Street.

items.title: Resolutions on Cradock Bridge Bus Stop Closure and Guardrail Repair
items.summary: The Council approved resolutions to request keeping the High and Main Street bus stop closed during bridge construction pending stakeholder review, and to repair a guardrail at Russell and Crane Streets.

items.title: Resolutions on Anti-Graffiti Ordinance and Monthly Budget Reporting
items.summary: The Council referred a proposed graffiti penalty ordinance update to subcommittee and passed a resolution requesting monthly budget-versus-actual reports from the administration.

items.title: Updates on Business Services and Health Department Inspections
items.summary: The Council received a written update on city business relations and approved a resolution recommending temporary inspector staffing to address a Board of Health inspection backlog.

items.title: Resolutions on Airport Noise, Malden Hospital Site, and Development Moratorium
items.summary: The Council requested updates on airport flight noise and Malden Hospital site plans, and referred a proposed building moratorium and comprehensive zoning review to committee.

items.title: Ordinance to Raise Legal Tobacco Purchase Age to 21
items.summary: The Council approved the first reading of an ordinance raising the legal age to purchase tobacco products in Medford to 21 after removing a proposed military exemption.

items.title: Condolences, Commendations, and Committee Reports
items.summary: The Council dedicated its session to former Mayor John McGlynn, passed several condolence and commendation resolutions, and referred committee reports on medical marijuana, food trucks, and taxi rules to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Petition for First Responders Monument
items.summary: Resident Jean Martin presented a proposal for a city monument honoring first responders, which the Council voted to receive and place on file.
